source_title: BTS & GOLD Guidelines: Triage and Acute Management of Adult Dyspnea, Asthma, and Pulmonary Embolism
issuing_authority: British Thoracic Society & Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease

chunks.section_header: Life-Threatening Respiratory Red Flags and Airway Obstruction
chunks.text_content: Any acute breathlessness accompanied by the following features mandates immediate emergency dispatch: Inspiratory stridor (high-pitched harsh breathing signaling upper airway compromise); inability to speak in complete phrases (sentence dyspnea); cyanosis (blue lips or tongue indicating SpO2 <85%); accessory muscle use with tracheal tug; silent chest on auscultation in severe bronchospasm; or acute hemoptysis accompanied by pleuritic chest pain and unilateral calf swelling (Wells score criteria indicating high clinical probability of Pulmonary Embolism).

chunks.section_header: Acute Exacerbation of Asthma and COPD Stratification
chunks.text_content: Severe acute asthma exacerbation is defined by PEFR (Peak Expiratory Flow Rate) 33-50% predicted, respiratory rate >=25 breaths/min, heart rate >=110 bpm, and inability to complete sentences. Moderate exacerbation exhibits PEFR 50-75% with stable vital signs. Immediate management: Inhaled short-acting beta-2 agonist (SABA, e.g. salbutamol/albuterol 4-10 puffs via spacer every 20 minutes) alongside systemic oral corticosteroids (prednisolone 40-50mg). Failure to achieve clinical improvement within 15-30 minutes mandates hospital transfer.
